evidence: Receiving DO2 steps from 11.52 mg/L (48.0 h) to 4.40 mg/L (48.2 h) and declines to 3.27 mg/L by 52.0 h
All three source batches held DO2 ≈ 10.5–11.5 mg/L during 48–52 h
Receiving P assay at 48 h = 3.27 g/L, comparable to sources (~3.0 g/L), same productive phase
minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; current DO2 ~3.3 and falling ~0.3 mg/L/h
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 crashed at 48.2 h from ~11.5 to ~4.4 mg/L while sources at the same clock held ~10.5–11.5 mg/L in the same productive phase (P ≈ 3.27 g/L at 48 h). DO2 is declining ~0.3 mg/L/h and will breach the 2.0 mg/L floor within ~4–5 h under KEEP. The combined intervention (feed 0.8×, air 1.15×) simultaneously cuts oxygen demand and raises supply, giving the largest margin against the oxygen-constraint violation among the bounded, non-terminal options, while retaining accumulated product mass and avoiding the zero-production stop. A single lever (increase_air or reduce_feed alone) provides less margin against a fault of this magnitude; strong_feed_reduction risks unnecessary productivity loss.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process parameters are unavailable; the root cause of the DO2 step crash (aeration equipment, back-pressure, viscosity) is unknown. If air capacity saturates, DO2 may still approach 2 mg/L and a stronger feed cut could become necessary. Product-quantity benefit of the 0.8 feed level is not directly measured — delayed assays lag by 4 h. Confidence that an intervention (rather than KEEP) is needed: high; confidence that 'combined' dominates 'increase_air': moderate.
